clean_story:
"Digital experiments. Predictions without risk.
The term computational modeling comes from using computers to simulate real-world systems, like testing a bridge’s strength before building it.

A weather forecast may seem simple, but behind it lies a model crunching temperature, pressure, and wind data across millions of grid points. Like rearranging a mosaic to predict tomorrow’s storm. Engineers use these models to design safer cars by simulating crashes in virtual space. Biologists map how diseases spread through populations, adjusting variables like vaccination rates to see outcomes. The precision comes from breaking problems into tiny, solvable pieces—then reassembling the answers. Supercomputers now run climate models with resolutions as fine as one kilometer, revealing local effects older tools missed.
Three related subjects are simulation accuracy, chaos theory and digital twins."
